__comment: Provisioned from deploy/grafana/dashboards/fulfilment.json. Edits made in the Grafana UI are discarded on restart — a dashboard that exists only in one person's browser is not a deliverable. Every panel answers a question somebody would ask during an incident; panels that only look busy were left out.
title: Order fulfilment

panels.title: Is the system doing its job?
Orders per minute, by outcome
panels.description: Confirmed versus cancelled. The single most useful panel: a rising cancellation rate is the first symptom of almost every failure in this system.

panels.title: Why orders were cancelled
panels.description: A rising share of INSUFFICIENT_STOCK is a business problem. A rising share of PAYMENT_ERROR or INTERNAL_ERROR is probably ours. A single 'cancelled' number cannot tell them apart, which is why the reason is a label.

panels.title: Stuck sagas
panels.description: A saga that could not compensate. It can go neither forward nor back, so it stops and waits for a human — this system never resolves that automatically. Should always be zero.

panels.title: Unresolved step outcomes
panels.description: Steps whose outcome is genuinely unknown — a call timed out and asking the callee did not settle it. The saga is waiting rather than guessing, which is correct, but a rising count means something is timing out and not recovering.

panels.title: Outbox backlog, by service
panels.description: Events written but not yet published. A backlog is not an error — it is the outbox absorbing a broker outage, which is what it is for. A backlog that stops FALLING is the problem.

panels.title: Saga step outcomes
panels.description: Every step attempt, by step and outcome. terminal_failure drives compensation; retryable_failure and unknown mean the saga is waiting. Reading this next to the traces in Jaeger is how a stalled order gets diagnosed.

panels.title: Saga step duration (p95)
panels.description: How long each step takes, including its network call. This is the measurement the reservation TTL has to be set against: if the sum of these approaches the TTL, healthy sagas will start failing at commit_reservation. See docs/sagas.md.

panels.title: Orders accepted
panels.description: Orders the API took. NOT sales: nothing is reserved and no money has moved at this point. The denominator for everything above.
